findings.claim: R-001 verification stage and VO continuity
findings.finding: The VP-001-v2 table assigns R-001 final due stage INTEGRATION_VALIDATION only if a separately approved integration rate/deadline exists. The detector-side obligation in corrected R-001 is independently binding: exactly one update for each legal accepted sample. VO-004-v2 provides implementation evidence for that detector obligation and declares verification_due_at IMPLEMENTATION. The VP and VO therefore assign conflicting due stages, leaving the detector obligation without an unambiguous stage in the plan.
findings.required_resolution: Revise VP-001-v2 so detector-side one-to-one accepted-sample processing has an explicit due stage consistent with VO-004-v2. Keep any future integration rate/deadline as a separate conditional requirement and VO, with its own owner and due stage. Do not change the current VO ledger or claim discharge in this correction.

findings.finding: The approved AP-002 selection protects one sample per millisecond and requires enforceable timing obligations. AS scope authority supersedes that algorithmic premise for the revised AS but explicitly leaves AP-002 and AD-003 as historical records whose applicability must be reviewed before downstream continuation. The authoring impact report identifies this conflict correctly; this review cannot reinterpret or supersede the AP authority.
findings.required_resolution: After correcting the verification-plan due-stage mismatch and obtaining an acceptable AS review, obtain an explicit engineering-authority disposition on AP-002 applicability or a superseding selection decision before establishing a new CON baseline. Keep AD-003 and all VO ledger entries unchanged pending authorized updates.

findings.required_resolution: Retain this as an external interface assumption. Define an integration owner, acceptance criterion, and evidence stage only if/when an integration contract is approved; do not convert it into a detector loss-detection requirement or claim it verified here.

reviewed_claims: The engineering scope decision supports newest-32 published samples in publication order and one detector update per accepted sample, independent of elapsed time.
The candidate keeps the unsigned 12-bit synthetic domain, approved 2048-byte detector-attributable SRAM scope, no-FPU constraint, exact newest-32 arithmetic, and no-overflow requirement.
The candidate does not impose physical loss detection, gap reconstruction, sequence tracking, watchdog behavior, or an unlimited-throughput guarantee on the detector.

PR-002 remains applicable to its abstract integer/ring recurrence, initialization, legal-value and one-update-per-input assumptions. Its accepted abstract mathematics does not establish C, publisher, timing, target, or firmware correctness.
